key_insight: LoViF 2026 (PhyScore) establishes that evaluating generated world-model videos requires a holistic metric beyond perceptual quality — jointly measuring multiple dimensions (e.g., perceptual fidelity, physical plausibility, temporal coherence, and input consistency) yields more meaningful assessments. The challenge provides a standardized benchmark and protocols to drive development of such multi‑dimensional metrics.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap where existing evaluation focuses on perceptual quality alone and fails to capture whether generated dynamics are physically plausible, temporally coherent, and consistent with conditioning inputs across both 2D and 4D generation settings.
method: Organize a public challenge (LoViF 2026 PhyScore) that asks participants to build a single metric predicting multiple quality dimensions for world‑model videos.
Provide a unified evaluation protocol and dataset spanning 2D and 4D generated videos, with multi‑dimensional ground truth (human/algorithmic annotations) for training and validation.

Score submissions on joint prediction accuracy and rank via an aggregated leaderboard to encourage holistic metric design (combining perceptual, physical, temporal, and conditional consistency checks).
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to evaluate generative world models with metrics that reflect real‑world usability (safety, realism, and consistency), accelerating progress in physically plausible and temporally coherent video generation. Standardized benchmarks reduce ambiguity and improve comparability of model improvements.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing inputs (2D/4D generators) → PhyScore metric → four output axes (perceptual, physical, temporal, consistency).
Radar/spider chart comparing metric scores across the four dimensions for sample models.
Before/after or side‑by‑side frame strips (2D vs 4D) annotated with PhyScore sub‑scores to illustrate failure modes.
Leaderboard bar chart showing top submissions and overall aggregated PhyScore for quick benchmarking.
paper_title: LoViF 2026 The First Challenge on Holistic Quality Assessment for 4D World Model (PhyScore)
paper_authors: Wei Luo, Yiting Lu, Xin Li, Haoran Li, Fengbin Guan
